New run TR-9120 (uuid 17578918) was read back two ways, neither trusting the clone's own inline response: get_test_runs_v1 shows TR-9120's overall_progress_by_status_id as a single bucket, {318615 (untested): count 5} — no passed/blocked buckets at all; get_test_cases_for_v1_test_run(TR-9120) shows all 5 rows with latest_status:'untested' and result_status.internal_name:'untested', including the two cases that carry real results on the source (TC-54485 -> mapping_id 2150424068, untested; TC-54486 -> mapping_id 2150424070, untested). So the clone reset every case to untested and did NOT copy TC-54485's Passed or TC-54486's Blocked result — this is correct, desirable behavior for a 're-execute the same scope' clone, not a defect.

DO NOT TRUST THE CLONE'S OWN RESPONSE — CONFIRMED AGAIN, SAME FAMILY AS clone_exploratory_session_v1. The 200 response returned inline by this very call reported test_cases_count:0, overall_progress all-zero ({untested:0,passed:0,...}), and overall_progress_by_status_id:{} — as if the clone were still empty. But get_test_runs_v1(TR-9120), read moments later, shows test_cases_count:5 and overall_progress_by_status_id:{318615:{count:5}}, and get_test_cases_for_v1_test_run(TR-9120) shows the 5 correct case identifiers already present (TC-54455, TC-54456, TC-54458, TC-54485, TC-54486 — exactly the source's case set). The case rows' own created_at (2026-09-22T05:29:46.685Z) is about 0.2s after the new run's created_at (05:29:46.500Z), so population was effectively synchronous — the clone's own response body is simply wrong/stale about what it had already finished doing, not slow. Unlike copy_folder, this capability declares no 'async' key at all in its response, so a caller has no signal that the inline numbers might be stale.

THREE-FIELD SERIALIZER — CLONE MATCHES create_test_run_v1 (CORRECT), NOT get_test_runs_v1/edit_test_run. In this call's own 200 body: project_id is the STRING "379335744" (correct), is_dynamic is the BOOLEAN false (correct), overall_progress is a real object with all seven status keys, zeroed (correct shape). Cross-checked against get_test_runs_v1 read of the SAME new run (TR-9120) moments later: project_id came back as a bare INTEGER 379335744 (wrong — declared string), is_dynamic came back as the INTEGER 0 (wrong — declared boolean), and overall_progress came back as null (wrong — declared object; not even an empty/zeroed object, actually null). The same three defects reproduce on TR-9110 itself in the same read. So clone_test_run's own write-response serializer is correct and consistent with create_test_run_v1; get_test_runs_v1 remains wrong on all three fields, now additionally confirmed to return outright null for overall_progress rather than a zeroed object, which is a slightly stronger defect than 'zeroed but present' would have been.
